transcript.content: Hello, I'm Dr. Smith. What brings you in today?

Hello Dr. Smith. I'm a 60-year-old school teacher currently transitioning into partial retirement, but instead of slowing down, I feel like I'm always on the go. Now that my days are less structured, I just can't seem to sit still and relax, even for a short visit or a quiet family meal.
Do you feel anxious only in specific situations, like when you're in public or around people, or does the anxiety happen even when you're alone at home?

It doesn't really feel like anxiety about being in public or around people. It's more of an inner restlessness and pent-up energy that hits me whenever I try to slow down or sit still. This happens both in social settings like my book club and when I'm just at home alone trying to read or watch a movie.
Have you been feeling down or losing interest in activities you used to enjoy, or is your main issue just the inability to relax and constant inner restlessness?

No, I don't feel down or lose interest at all—I've actually been very active with gardening, community events, and workshops. The real issue is this constant inner restlessness and feeling like I'm always on the go. It's just incredibly frustrating that I can't seem to sit still and relax when I actually want to.
Do you ever feel unusually energetic, need less sleep than usual, or find your thoughts racing more than normal?

No, I don't experience racing thoughts, and my sleep has been completely normal. It doesn't feel like an unusually high or manic energy, but rather a constant physical restlessness and an inability to just sit still. It's more about my body needing to move than my mind spinning.
Have you noticed any involuntary movements, like tremors, twitching, or a feeling of shakiness in your limbs, especially when you're at rest?
No, I haven't noticed any involuntary tremors, twitching, or shakiness in my limbs at all. Any movement I make is just me fidgeting or needing to get up, rather than my body shaking on its own.
